newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris blasts Louisiana action.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris blasts Louisiana action.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc said the Louisiana attorney general's petition naming more than 100 insurance companies as defendants in the state's tobacco litigation was an "obvious act of desperation."

"The attorney general's attempt to add the insurance comanies appears to be nothing more than an attempt to divert attention from the baseless nature of the underlying lawsuit," Philip Morris senior assistant general counsel Gregory Little said.
Philip Morris said it has not submitted any claims to its insurers in connection with the state's lawsuit against it.
Philip Morris also said it does not believe it is appropriate to add them to this litigation.
The Louisiana attorney general named more than 100 insurance companies as defendants in litigation against the tobacco industry in an effort to recover "billions" in Medicaid costs.
The petition was filed March 14 in Louisiana's 14th Judicial District Court.
Insurance companies named included American International Group Inc, The Hartford, Lloyds of London, ACE Ltd, EXEL Ltd and Continental Corp, which was bought by CNA Financial Corp.
CNA Financial said it was reviewing the legal documents and had no immediate comment. American International Group declined comment.

The Hartford said it has not yet received legal notification about the action and said the state's petition "appears to us to be part of the ongoing legal dispute between Louisiana and the manufacturers."
A Lloyd's spokesman in New York had no immediate comment.
